title: Saudi Qualification Verification Disruptions Slow Work Visa Processing, Fragomen Warns
excerpt: The pre-entry degree-verification step for Saudi work visas is taking longer than usual, with some applications returned for resubmission and no official timeline for a fix — a delay that lands heavily on Indian recruits.
body:
• Saudi Arabia's Qualification Verification Program (QVP) — the pre-entry check of educational qualifications required for work visa applicants — is experiencing disruptions across multiple jurisdictions, immigration law firm Fragomen has alerted employers.
  • Processing may take longer than usual, and some applications are being returned or require resubmission. The extent of the delays and the timeline for resolving them remain unclear.
  • The QVP step normally adds about 15 days to a Saudi work visa timeline and carries a government fee of USD 93, on top of which applicants must now budget extra time.
  • Anyone mid-application — including the large number of Indian professionals recruited for Saudi jobs — should confirm their verification status with their employer or sponsor before making travel or joining plans.

Foreign nationals applying for Saudi Arabian work visas are facing delays at the qualification-verification stage, according to an alert from immigration law firm Fragomen. The Qualification Verification Program (QVP), which requires applicants for Work Visas and Temporary Work Visas to have their educational qualifications verified before they enter Saudi Arabia, is currently experiencing disruptions across multiple jurisdictions. Processing may take longer than usual, some applications are being returned or are requiring resubmission, and — in Fragomen's words — the extent of the delays and the anticipated timeline for resolution remain unclear.

What the QVP is, and who it touches

The QVP is part of Saudi Arabia's Professional Accreditation programme, run by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Its purpose, as the ministry describes it, is to ensure expatriate workers hold reliable academic qualifications that match the occupation they are entering, checked against the Saudi standard classifications of occupations and educational levels before the worker arrives. What began as a programme for countries without a Saudi cultural attaché has since expanded: based on practitioner experience, Fragomen has reported that the QVP requirement now applies across all industry sectors, with applicants required to obtain a Professional Accreditation Certificate through the QVP portal before their visa can proceed.

That scope is what makes a disruption at this stage significant. The QVP is not an optional extra: it sits on the critical path of the work visa, normally extending the overall application timeline by about 15 days and carrying a government fee of USD 93. Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian workforces in the Gulf, and Indian recruits — engineers, healthcare staff, IT professionals, technicians and corporate hires — pass through this verification in large numbers.

What applicants and employers should do

Fragomen's advice is directed mainly at employers: factor additional processing time into recruitment and onboarding plans. For applicants, the practical consequences follow from the alert itself. A verification that would normally clear in about 15 days may now take longer; an application that is returned will need to be resubmitted, restarting that clock; and joining dates, travel bookings and resignation timings built on the old timeline are exposed until the verification clears. Applicants mid-process should confirm the current status of their QVP case with their employer or sponsor — the party that manages the visa file — before acting on any of those dates.

What is not yet known

The disruption is reported on the basis of Fragomen's practitioner experience across jurisdictions; Saudi Arabia's MHRSD has not published a statement on the disruptions, their cause, or a date by which normal processing is expected to resume. Until the ministry or the QVP portal operator says otherwise, applicants and employers should treat the standard 15-day verification window as a floor rather than a planning figure, and watch for an official update.
